root_idea.summary: The root combines extended or unlimited duration with withdrawal into wildness, estrangement, or human avoidance.
root_idea.development: Its duration branch yields expressions for permanence, eternity, and lastingness; its wildness branch develops into meanings of becoming untamed, avoiding people, deserted places, and figurative strangeness.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested group is the temporal adverb أَبَدًا and is displayed under that normalized lexical form.

senses.definition: Ever; forever; throughout all future time.
senses.usage_conditions: A temporal adverb expressing continuance through the future. In affirmative contexts it commonly means “forever,” while with negation it commonly means “never”; these are contextual uses of the same temporal sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain, stay, abide, or dwell constantly or permanently in a place without leaving it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participle آبِدٌ describes one who remains or dwells continually.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become wild, take fright, flee, or shun human beings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the verb describing a transition into the behavior of a wild animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To use strange, unfamiliar, or obscure words or phrases in poetry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is figurative and concerns expressions that are not readily intelligible.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become angry with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction أَبِدَ عَلَيْهِ means “he was angry with him.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or render perpetual.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In an idiomatic negative expression, تأبيدًا can refer to doing a deed destined ever to be remembered or mentioned.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause a beast to take fright, become wild, or flee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a causative counterpart to the intransitive wildness branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain long away from home; to remain long celibate and become little in need or desire of women.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meanings describe prolonged estrangement or withdrawal from ordinary social and domestic life.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become deserted, as a place, and come to be inhabited by wild animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject is a place of abode or sojourning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Time or duration, especially a long, unlimited, or indivisible span; endless time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may denote prospective eternity or an extended duration. Its plural forms can designate portions of time or intensify the meaning in particular expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Everlasting or enduring without end; by substantivization, the Everlasting, and in one usage the Ancient without beginning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are substantive or theological uses of the noun rather than the adverbial Quranic form أَبَدًا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Offspring that is one year old.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct nominal usage recorded in Classical Arabic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unsocial, unfamiliar, shy, or wild like a wild animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is applied to people and to animals that shun or avoid human company.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A prolific female that breeds or gives birth abundantly, especially one that bears yearly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is applied to a female slave, she-ass, mare, or she-camel in the cited lexical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Everlastingness: the quality of unlimited, indivisible, or endless duration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes the abstract quality of perpetual duration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sayings formulated as expressions of perpetuity or indefinite continuance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional plural term for sayings expressing that something will continue without end.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wild animal that shuns and takes fright at human beings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural أَوَابِدُ is also used in قَيْدُ الأَوَابِدِ for a swift or active horse able to overtake wild animals, and in a proverb for benefits understood as fleeting. The designation is also associated with wild animals’ naturally enduring for a long or seemingly unlimited time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A deed, calamity, or formidable, strange, or evil event remembered because of its extraordinary or grievous nature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is used of something people find alarming or worthy of lasting mention.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A strange, unusual, unfamiliar, or obscure word, saying, rhyme, verse, or poem.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is figurative for language remote from ordinary intelligibility or for extraordinary poetic compositions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Made or rendered perpetual.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe property made an unalienable endowment for pious uses, not to be sold or inherited.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wild, intractable, or unmanageable she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This feminine participial usage is applied specifically to the cited animal.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only cross-reference to the Form I entry.
The active-participle staying sense is covered by the broader permanent-dwelling meaning.
Pointer-only reference to expressions under أَبَدٌ.

cautions: The Quranic form أَبَدًا is the temporal adverb; the related noun أَبَدٌ and the wildness, animal, and perpetuity branches are listed separately rather than treated as senses of every occurrence.
English “ever,” “never,” and “forever” reflect the surrounding affirmative or negative construction and do not require separate Quranic senses.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: Maqayis records the terse expression تَأَبَّدَ وَجْهُهُ كَلِفَ, but the exact interpretation of كَلِفَ is not sufficiently clear from the supplied context to establish a separate meaning; the independently supported wildness and anger branches are represented.
